title: The Tortoise and the Hare
source: Aesop's Fables（公有領域原著，自家簡化改寫）
paragraphs: A hare lived near a quiet forest. He was very fast, and he liked to tell every animal about it. One day he saw a tortoise walking slowly along the path and began to laugh at him.
"You are so slow," the hare said. "I could run around this whole field before you take ten steps." The tortoise looked up calmly. "Maybe so," he said. "But why not race and find out? I am ready now."

The other animals heard about the race and came to watch. A fox agreed to stand at the finish line and decide the winner. The hare and the tortoise stood at the start, and the fox gave a signal. The race began.

The hare jumped far ahead in just a few seconds. Soon he could not even see the tortoise behind him. He felt very proud of himself. "This race is too easy," he thought. "I have plenty of time to rest." He found a soft spot under a tree and lay down.

The hare closed his eyes, planning to rest for only a minute. But he was tired from running so fast, and soon he was sleeping deeply. Meanwhile, the tortoise kept walking. He did not run, and he did not stop. He simply moved forward, one slow step after another.
The tortoise finally reached the tree where the hare was sleeping. He did not wake him or say a word. He just kept going, past the tree and closer to the finish line, step by step under the warm sun.

The hare slept for a long time. The sun moved low in the sky before he finally woke up. He jumped up in fear and ran as fast as he could toward the finish line. But he arrived too late, and there he saw the tortoise already standing next to the fox, who was smiling.
The hare had lost the race. From that day, he never laughed at anyone again. Slow and steady wins the race.
